rows.evidence: Rule (BUILDER_RULES 5; VERIFIER_RULES 2.3): a B or C claim must cite its published counter-evidence if any exists; a FAIL needs a named published source that contests the claim and that the page omits. The claim is C ('a measurable fraction of funds outperform the market'). Published contests found and read (abstracts quoted in row R25-hounyo-counter-search): (1) Barras, Scaillet and Wermers (2010, JF 65(1)) - cited in the span, with its 75% zero-alpha result (net of expenses) and 'almost none by 2006'. (2) Andrikogiannopoulou and Papakonstantinou (2019, JF 74(5)) - cited in the span as the contest of (1): 'this methodology is conservative and underestimates the proportion of nonzero-alpha funds'. That paper supports the Hounyo claim, so it is a rebuttal of the counter, which the span shows on both sides. (3) Fama and French (2010, JF 65(5); registry fama2010luck, used_by AP8 and FC3, not S7) - not cited on L06. Its abstract: 'Bootstrap simulations suggest that few funds produce benchmark-adjusted expected returns sufficient to cover their costs. If we add back the costs in fund expense ratios, there is evidence of inferior and superior performance (nonzero true alpha) in the extreme tails.' This is a net-of-cost contest in magnitude ('few funds'), but a measurable fraction is also compatible with 'few', and the same abstract reports nonzero alpha in the tails gross of costs, which supports the claim. It is therefore not a flat contest of the span's claim, and the span already presents the net-of-cost contest through Barras et al. Judgement on the merits: the span as written presents the claim, a named published contest with its finding, and the published reply to that contest, which is two-sided treatment; omitting Fama and French (2010) does not make the treatment one-sided. No 2025-26 contest found in the citing-works search (R25-hounyo-counter-search) is omitted. Architect note (not a failure): fama2010luck would be a second, corroborating citation once S7 is in its used_by list. Result: PASS.

Mills-ratio bounds (Lemma 2.2): x phi(x)/(1 + x^2) <= Q(x) <= phi(x)/x give phi(z) <= Q(z)(z + 1/z) and phi(z)/Q(z) >= z, so e^(-z^2/2) = sqrt(2 pi) phi(z) <= sqrt(pi/2) p (z + 1/z) and it suffices that u(z) = -ln p - c(z + 1/z) >= 0 (page's steps; -ln p = -ln 2 - ln Q, Q' = -phi, so u' = phi/Q - c(1 - 1/z^2)). u' >= z - c(1 - 1/z^2) > 0 for all z > 0 (for z < 1 the right side is negative; for z >= 1 it is below c < 1 <= z), so u is increasing. At p = 1/e, z* = 0.9004526 and u(z*) = 1 - c(z* + 1/z*) = 0.0727888 > 0 (scipy). The page's displayed arithmetic 1 - 0.46107 x 2.01101 = 0.0728 (exact 0.072789 -> 0.0728). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html Lab 6 hypothesis (line 722) and interpretation (line 873): 'On the same bootstrap draws, a maximum over more rules is at least as large, so every family-wide critical value below is at most the one the full search would need'
rows.evidence: unchanged since c16bcf1 (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-derived. Fix the bootstrap draws (the same index vectors). For rule sets A subset of A', the max over A' of the centred t*_k is pointwise at least the max over A. Hence the (1 - alpha) quantile over the draws of the max over A' is at least that over A, so a critical value computed on the 30 rules is at most the one for any larger universe (and StepM's step-1 critical value is non-decreasing in the number of rules). The argument uses only the definition of the maximum and of the empirical quantile. Numerical check (subset_quantile.py; the twin's draws: seed 507, mean block 10, B = 1000): the 95% quantile of the max of the centred t* over the first m rules is 2.1404 (m = 5), 2.4525 (10), 2.6475 (15), 2.8040 (20), 2.8178 (25) and 2.8371 (all 30; this is the twin's StepM first step, 2.837). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L05.html lines 596-598 (equicorrelated normals are MTP2 for 0 <= rho < 1; one-sided p-values; the Simes step at line 598), Lab 5 hypothesis (line 638)
rows.evidence: unchanged since c16bcf1 (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-derived at d10fb51. (a) Sigma = (1-rho) I + rho 11' with Sherman-Morrison: Sigma^{-1} = (1/(1-rho)) [I - rho 11'/(1-rho+m0 rho)], so the off-diagonal entries of Q are -rho/((1-rho)(1-rho+m0 rho)) <= 0 for 0 <= rho < 1. (b) For a normal density with precision Q, log f(z) = const - (1/2) z'Qz; with u = x v y and v = x ^ y, u_i^2 + v_i^2 = x_i^2 + y_i^2, so the diagonal terms cancel and log f(u) + log f(v) - log f(x) - log f(y) = (1/2) sum_{i != j} Q_ij (x_i x_j + y_i y_j - u_i u_j - v_i v_j). The bracket is 0 when (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) >= 0 and equals (x_i - y_i)(x_j - y_j) <= 0 otherwise (checked in the four sign cases), so each term Q_ij times the bracket is >= 0 and f(u) f(v) >= f(x) f(y). Numerical spot check (num/simes_mtp2_check.out): 200,000 random pairs for each of (m, rho) = (3, 0.2), (5, 0.7), (10, 0.95), (20, 0): min(lhs - rhs) = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, -1.4e-14 (rounding), violations 0. (c) One-sided p-values are decreasing in z coordinatewise, which swaps join and meet, and the Jacobian is a product of one-coordinate factors that cancels because {u_i, v_i} = {x_i, y_i}: the true-null p-values are MTP2 as the page says. PASS.

rows.evidence: unchanged since c16bcf1 (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Derivation, written out and checked: (1) Lab 5's true-null statistics are z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j with mu_j = 0 (the lab code: z = sqrt(rho) w + sqrt(1-rho) e + mu), p_j = 1 - Phi(z_j), rho in [0,1): this is Proposition 5.3's model restricted to the nulls, so the true-null p-values are PRDS on every subset (Definition 5.1). (2) Theorem 5.2's hypotheses hold for the family of the m0 true-null p-values (the family is all true nulls, so PRDS on the true nulls is PRDS on the family; each p_j is super-uniform because z_j ~ N(0,1) gives p_j ~ U(0,1); P(p_j <= u) = u > 0 for u > 0). Its bound FDR <= m0' q / m' with m' = m0' = m0 gives FDR <= q = alpha for BH at level alpha on the family. (3) When every hypothesis in the family is true, V = R, so FDR = E[1{R >= 1}] = P(R >= 1). (4) BH at level alpha on m0 p-values (step-up) rejects at least one hypothesis iff q_(l) <= l alpha/m0 for some l <= m0. Hence P(union_{l<=m0} {q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}) <= alpha: the Simes inequality for the true-null p-values. (5) Theorem 7.5 (containment {FDP > gamma} subset of union_{l<=M}{q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}, M <= m0, for the step-down with constants (3)) gives P(FDP > gamma) <= alpha for every rho in [0,1). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html line 330 ('Exchangeability is assumed, not justified. Bonferroni, Holm and BHY treat every hypothesis alike.') and the Section 6 normal-approximation paragraph
rows.evidence: unchanged since c16bcf1 (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Classified at 3203b7e as definitional. 'Bonferroni, Holm and BHY treat every hypothesis alike' follows from Definition 2.1 and the step-down and step-up rules (the procedures use the p-values only through their ranks and the values of the statistics; the threshold of Bonferroni is the same at every step). 'Neither holds exactly for small samples, fat tails or serially correlated predictor returns' is a statement about the asymptotic normal approximation (Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.3 are asymptotic in the normal approximation; the MBF formula assumes the normal test statistic). Neither is an empirical or literature claim, so neither needs a span under the page's convention, and neither carries a number. PASS.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L06.html Theorem 4.2 (lines 256-260, proof at 262-266) and the Problem P-solution at line ~405 (the same bound at π0 = 0.99)
rows.evidence: unchanged since c16bcf1 (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-derived at bda7c27. Assumptions: Z ~ N(θ,1), H0: θ = 0, prior π_A on θ under the alternative (Definition 4.1). Step 1: φ(z−θ) ≤ φ(0) for every θ, so ∫φ(z−θ)π_A(dθ) ≤ φ(0) and B(π_A) = φ(z)/∫φ(z−θ)π_A(dθ) ≥ φ(z)/φ(0) = e^(−z²/2); the point mass at θ = z attains it. Step 2: posterior odds of H0 = PO·B(π_A) ≥ PO·e^(−z²/2); x ↦ x/(1+x) is increasing, so (4) holds. Numerical check (c096_check_r22.out): at z = 3, π0 = 0.99: PO = 99, x = PO·MBF = 1.099790657286, x/(1+x) = 0.523762049074; the threshold PO* = e^4.5 = 90.0171313005 gives π0* = 0.9890130574. Alternative priors (part B): B(π_A) ≥ MBF = 0.011108996538 for all 11 structured priors and all 2000 random discrete priors; the point mass gives B − MBF = 0 to floating point. Scope note checked: Definition 4.1 takes π_A as any prior on θ under the alternative and does not exclude θ = 0; on that reading the point mass δ_z attains the bound for every z, including z = 0 (B = 1 = e^0). If the alternative were meant to exclude θ = 0, attainment would hold for z ≠ 0 only, and the infimum would be approached, not attained, at z = 0; the Bayes figure at t = 0 shows the MBF as 1.00, which is the infimum on either reading. The proof's steps are complete and the assumptions are stated. PASS.
